what: Every accepted answer in a published artifact, screened for a name the gold does not state — the judge audit's 44.90% entity-swap rate applied to all 500 rows instead of to 49 sampled cases.
why: §13.184 measured the judge accepting 19.38% of answers that were wrong by construction, and split it: entity-swap 44.90%, number-swap 14.75%, cross-gold 0/50. A rate over 160 cases does not say which capability carries it, and the campaign's head-to-head is MR. This screen answers that from the artifact, with no model and no key.

artifact.why: the artifact the campaign is currently read from

workflow: mr-entity-recheck.yml dispatched with run_id=41159983913, capability=MR (GitHub run 41177330482)

discrimination.reading: the screen fires 5.2x more often on answers the judge rejected than on the ones it accepted, so it is not blind — but at 1.2% it is far below the 19.38% the audit measured, which is the first sign that the audit's rate is not a per-answer property

verdict: the screen does not reach MR

predictions.name: the registered one
predictions.registered: MR first-round accepted count after the screen is at most 84 - 5 = 79, i.e. at least 5 accepted answers name something the gold does not name
predictions.measured: 0 candidates, so the count stays at 84

predictions.name: why it failed
predictions.measured: 82 of the 84 accepted MR golds name nothing at all: they are 2, $50, 20%, 3 days, $5,850, 140 hours. The screen's reach on MR is 2 of 84 = 2.4%
predictions.verdict: the falsification is informative rather than null

predictions.name: the audit's population
predictions.measured: 119 of 419 accepted answers name anything, so the 44.90% entity-swap rate is a statement about at most those 119 — and MR contributes 2 of them
predictions.verdict: the 19.38% cannot be attributed to MR on name evidence

withdrawn: The previous iteration annotated MR's 87.25 as 'judge-limited' by multiplying 19.38% x 121 = 23.5 questions. This reading removes the premise: MR golds carry no names, so entity-swap cases could not be drawn from MR, and the rate is about the other capabilities. §13.186 replaces the annotation with a measurement on the channel MR does have.
defectsFound: The first version of `sourcesFrom` filtered on `typeof question.answer === 'string'`, which dropped every decline: 8 of MR's 121 rows vanished and the reading still looked whole, because a decline is never correct and the numerator was untouched. Fixed; the second reading counts 121 MR rows.

The audit's own stoplist read `Five` in the gold `Five months ago` as a name, and the screen listed a false accept on a question about duration. Pronouns, discourse markers and number words are now excluded (§13.185).
limits: The screen compares capitalised words. A gold whose only content is a list of common nouns (`a tent, a sleeping bag`) is unreachable, which is 300 of 419 accepted rows in this artifact.

An answer that names nothing but is wrong (`2 people` against a gold naming Alice and Bob) is `unnamed-answer`, a published relation rather than a pass. The candidate count is a lower bound, never an estimate.

A candidate is a candidate: 1 of the 5 listed on `all` is a correct abridged answer (`Screen protectors, phone wallet cases` against a gold about an `iPhone 13 Pro`). The list is for adjudication, not for subtraction.
It does not measure the judge. It measures which real answers exercise the channel the judge was shown to miss.
